periods.label: From Gutenberg to Westphalia
periods.note: A political settlement: the Thirty Years’ War ends.

periods.label: From Gutenberg to the end of English licensing
periods.note: A change in press control, in one country.

periods.label: From Luther to Westphalia
periods.note: The shorter clock starts with the Reformation.

chapters.title: Print spreads
events: The starting point here is movable-type printing in Europe.
Printing spreads across Europe during the first half-century.
A landmark of the new printing process.
Print becomes a vehicle for religious controversy. This is the alternative start of the adjustment clock.

chapters.title: Conflict and control
events: Religious and political upheaval turns violent.
The Catholic Church organizes its response to the Reformation.
Formal Catholic censorship attempts to control what circulates.
Decades of conflict; the St. Bartholomew’s Day Massacre follows in 1572.
The long conflict that makes 1648 one possible endpoint.

chapters.title: Settlements, not a finish line
events: Ends the Thirty Years’ War. A political settlement, not the end of every religious conflict.
Pre-publication licensing regulates the English press.
The licensing system expires — a liberalization; other restrictions on publication remain.
Britain establishes statutory copyright with limited terms.
The United States gives freedom of the press constitutional protection.

source_mermaid:
timeline
    title From Mainz to a settled press
    1450 : Gutenberg's press at Mainz : Movable type in Europe
    1455 : The Gutenberg Bible
    1450-1500 : The incunabula period : Book prices fall by two-thirds : Presses spread across Europe
    1517 : Luther's 95 Theses : Presses in 200+ European cities. The first viral text
    1524-1525 : German Peasants' War : ~100,000 dead
    1545-1563 : Council of Trent : The institutional counter-move
    1559 : Index Librorum Prohibitorum : Formal Catholic censorship
    1562-1598 : French Wars of Religion : 2-4 million dead
    1572 : St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre
    1618-1648 : Thirty Years' War : 4.5-8 million dead : German lands lose 20-35% of population
    1648 : Peace of Westphalia : Confessional settlement
    1662 : English Licensing Act : State pre-publication control
    1695 : Licensing Act lapses : England ends pre-publication censorship
    1710 : Statute of Anne : Copyright as we know it
    1791 : First Amendment
